summary: Iteration 4 (restoration milestones + value-score badges) verified. Backend 9/9 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_milestones_iter4.py: GET /api/config exposes restoration_milestones (4 entries: 25/Old Clock Tower/+150/+5%, 50/Rail Station/+350/+5%, 75/River Bridge/+600/+5%, 100/Grand Town Hall/+1000/+10%), and contracts.value_score (w_coins=1.0, w_xp=1.2, w_restoration=8.0, w_materials=1.0, w_time=0.2, premium_threshold=380, unit_time_seconds scrap=10/comp=40/finished=110). Save/load round-trip preserves state.claimed_milestones ([25,50], [], and [25,50,75,100] verified). Frontend Town Hall shows landmarks-section with 4 skyline tiles (all locked at 0 pts) and 4 landmark rows with correct '+X% rewards · +Y coins' text and 'N pts' status. Via dev tools (grant level ×5 + grant materials ×10 + repeated Fulfil Order) restoration reached 100/100; all 4 milestones triggered a landmark toast in order (Clock Tower→Rail Station→River Bridge→Grand Town Hall) and skyline tiles flipped to skyline-<pts>-unlocked. Contract reward numbers scaled up after buff: Industrial (3 goods) went from +57c/+29 XP pre-buff to +75c/+46 XP after +25% total buff. Value-score badges: on the 3-card board best_value + quick_cash pills appeared, at most one best_value across cards, no duplicate badge type — matches spec. ONE UX BUG FOUND: milestone toast duplicates 2-3× per crossing (Clock Tower toasted at 3 consecutive fulfils even though claimed_milestones should gate it) — root cause is showToast() being called inside the setState functional updater in fulfillContract, so React StrictMode double-invokes and the toast side-effect fires each time. Coin bonus itself is NOT double-paid (React keeps only the final next state). Emergency-card 'no value badge' assertion could not be run to completion in-browser because a Town Hall Restored! modal covered the board after restoration hit 100 — verified by code inspection instead (EmergencyCard has no badge testID). Regression: full loop (scrap → machine shop → contracts → dev tools → reset) still works.

ui_bugs.issue: Milestone toast '🏛 <landmark> restored! +N coins' fires 2-3 times for the same landmark on consecutive fulfils. Repro: reach 25 restoration on fulfil #A → toast; on fulfil #A+1 (restoration=e.g. 35, milestone 25 already claimed) → SAME Clock Tower toast fires again. Coins are correct (single bonus). Root cause: showToast() is invoked inside setState((prev)=>{...}) — StrictMode double-invokes and the impure side-effect runs each pass. Move showToast + haptic OUT of the setState updater (compute a 'landmarkUnlocked' local and fire the toast after setState, e.g. via a useEffect on claimed_milestones length). Reference: /app/frontend/src/game/GameContext.tsx:319-330

issues: 'Town Hall Restored!' modal covers the whole board with no visible close/backdrop-tap; only the 'Keep Building' button dismisses it. Consider adding backdrop-tap-to-dismiss.

critical_code_review_comments: GameContext.fulfillContract: side-effects (showToast, haptic, setLevelUpFlash) live INSIDE the setState functional updater. In StrictMode/dev this fires twice per action; in prod it's still an anti-pattern. Move to useEffect on derived state.
engine.contractBadges early-returns {} when contracts.length < 2 — correct, but with board_size=3 in config this is fine; document assumption.

engine.contractBadges: argmaxId uses initial 'best' element without reduce accumulator seed — works but silently returns first-in-tie. Ties on efficiency/score are common with generated integers; consider deterministic tie-breaking (e.g., higher score wins, then higher coins).

rca_of_issue: Duplicate milestone toast root cause: showToast() is called inside the setState functional updater in fulfillContract. React StrictMode intentionally double-invokes updaters to detect impure reducers; each pass re-fires the setToast side-effect, producing 2-3 visible toasts per single fulfil that crosses a threshold. State itself (claimed_milestones, coins) is correct because React only commits the final 'next'. Fix: hoist toast/haptic out of the reducer — compute a payload inside setState (or via a state diff useEffect on claimed_milestones.length) and trigger showToast + haptic exactly once per commit.
